title: A Gradient-based yet Spike-Timing-Dependent Solution to the Feedback Learning Problem in Neural Microcircuits
abstract: arXiv:2609.08070v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The brain uses discrete spikes for dynamic computation, yet, how neural microcircuits (NMCs) solve temporal credit assignment using local spike timing remains a fundamental open question. Dominant spiking neural network (SNN) approaches circumvent this by approximating backpropagation through surrogate gradients, decoupling learning from biological spike timing. Here, we reformulate temporal credit assignment as a state separation problem: extracting task-required components induced by historical perturbations directly from the current neural state. This enables an online feedback learning framework for NMCs through a gradient tunneling (GT) algorithm and the lead-lag expansion technique that derives credit assignment from local synaptic spike timing, while remaining compatible with ANN-SNN hybrid architectures. translated_title: 一种基于梯度但依赖脉冲时序的神经微回路反馈学习问题解决方案
translated_abstract: 大脑利用离散脉冲进行动态计算，然而神经微回路如何利用局部脉冲时序来解决时间信用分配问题仍然是一个基本的开放性问题。主流的脉冲神经网络（SNN）方法通过代理梯度近似反向传播来规避这一问题，使学习与生物脉冲时序解耦。在此，我们将时间信用分配重新表述为一个状态分离问题：直接从当前神经状态中提取由历史扰动引起的任务所需成分。这使得通过梯度隧穿（GT）算法和超前-滞后展开技术，为神经微回路构建了在线反馈学习框架，该技术从局部突触脉冲时序中推导信用分配，同时保持与ANN-SNN混合架构的兼容性。实验表明，经GT训练的神经微回路在长时间尺度的证据整合和抗噪记忆保持方面表现出色，并且能够执行……
tldr: 本文提出梯度隧穿算法，将时间信用分配重构为状态分离问题，从局部突触脉冲时序推导信用分配，实现了与生物脉冲时序一致的神经微回路在线反馈学习框架。
